::: {.purpose}
**Why read this.** Sessions 1–6 used one condition, equal chemical potential, with six kinds of model and data. Session 7 asks one question of all of them: what evidence would make you trust the result? Use this guide to review, then bring the one topic you feel least ready for.
:::

## 1. One condition, six forms

| Session | Equilibrium | Working equation | Model in it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 · VLE, flash | vapor–liquid | y<sub>i</sub>Φ<sub>i</sub>P = x<sub>i</sub>γ<sub>i</sub>P<sub>i</sub><sup>sat</sup>; Rachford–Rice | γ, P<sup>sat</sup> |
| 2 · measured VLE | same, solved for γ | γ<sub>i</sub> = y<sub>i</sub>Φ<sub>i</sub>P/(x<sub>i</sub>P<sub>i</sub><sup>sat</sup>) | G<sup>E</sup> model, weights |
| 3 · LLE | liquid–liquid | x<sub>i</sub><sup>α</sup>γ<sub>i</sub><sup>α</sup> = x<sub>i</sub><sup>β</sup>γ<sub>i</sub><sup>β</sup>; TPD ≥ 0 | NRTL τ(T) |
| 4 · solids, surfaces | solid–liquid; gas–surface | ln(x₁γ₁) = −(Δ<sub>fus</sub>H/R)(1/T − 1/T<sub>m</sub>); n = PV/RT + mq | fusion data, W; isotherm |
| 5 · reactions | chemical | Πa<sub>i</sub><sup>ν<sub>i</sub></sup> = K(T), ln K = −Δ<sub>r</sub>G°/RT | H(T), S(T), K<sub>φ</sub> |
| 6 · cells | electrochemical | Δ<sub>r</sub>G = −nFE; a<sub>KCl</sub> = (mγ±)² | Debye–Hückel, B, C |

## 2. What decided each answer

Each session had a result that looked right and was not, and the evidence that showed it.

| Session | Looked right | Evidence that decided |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | Weighted NRTL fit, RMS(r/σ) = 1.16 | It predicts a liquid split (0.088–0.237) in a miscible mixture |
| 3 | Exact fit to one tie line | Held-out tie lines: RMSE 0.077 with constant τ, 0.0097 with τ = a + b/T |
| 4 | W = +238 J/mol for naphthalene in benzene | With the other fusion data, W = −522 J/mol; the solubility prediction is the same |
| 5 | A solver that converged | K from constant Δ<sub>r</sub>H gives 0.498 conversion; the correct K gives 0.795 |
| 6 | A good fit of γ± | The cell needs (mγ±)²; with mγ± every EMF is half |

## 3. The evidence ladder

From weakest to strongest:

1. **Calibration:** the model reproduces the data it was fitted to. Two equations, two parameters: always possible.
2. **Internal consistency:** Gibbs–Duhem, element balances, TPD ≥ 0 at the fitted phases.
3. **Held-out data:** same kind of measurement, conditions the fit did not use.
4. **Independent property:** a different quantity the model also predicts, such as LLE from a VLE fit, or H<sup>E</sup> from τ(T).
5. **Different method:** calorimetry against EMF, DSC against solubility.

A claim is only as strong as the highest rung it reached. Extrapolation beyond the data, such as the 324 K closing of the cyclohexane–methanol gap, reaches none.

## 4. Checking code you did not write line by line

From Session 2 you have used AI assistants to write code. The checks that caught real errors in this course were:

- a quantity recomputed independently (P<sup>sat</sup>, ln K, an activity);
- a balance that must close (atoms, moles, O/C ratio);
- a limit the answer must satisfy (0 &lt; β &lt; 1, x<sup>α</sup> ≠ x<sup>β</sup>, TPD at w = z equals 0);
- the objective re-evaluated at the reported parameters;
- a known case reproduced (the Lab E reference values).

Convergence and a small residual check the solver, not the thermodynamics.

## 5. Before Session 7

1. For each session, write the one equation you would use first and the one assumption you would check first.
2. Pick one result from your own lab files and place it on the evidence ladder.
3. Bring the topic you feel least ready for. The exit-ticket form has a field for it.
